blocks.text: 2 Samuel 14 contains 33 verses. It opens with: Now Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king's heart was toward Absalom. It concludes with: So Joab came to the king, and told him; and when he had called for Absalom, he came to the king, and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king: and the king kissed Absalom. Supplied contextual evidence for this passage adds: Second Samuel moves from David's accession and kingdom consolidation through ark and dynasty promise to royal abuse, household violence, rebellion, grief, and a four-part closing appendix.
